job.style: a comparison of two related ideas

response.passage: Light behaves in fascinating ways as it travels through our world. First, light always travels in a straight line, which is why it cannot bend around corners to reach behind a wall. When light hits an object, it creates a shadow only if there is a screen or surface behind the object to catch the blocked light. Without a surface, the shadow has nowhere to form. Second, we must distinguish between how objects interact with light. A luminous object, like a glowing bulb, produces its own light. In contrast, the Moon is non-luminous because it merely reflects sunlight rather than creating its own. Furthermore, materials interact with light differently based on their properties. Transparent materials allow light to pass through completely, while translucent materials allow only some light to pass, making objects on the other side look blurry. Opaque materials block light entirely. Interestingly, reflection is not limited to mirrors; almost every surface around us reflects light, which is how we see objects in the first place. Even a rough wall reflects light, though it does not create a clear image like a polished mirror does. Understanding these simple rules helps us explain everything from the dark patches on the ground to the bright glow of the night sky.
response.summary: Light travels in straight lines and interacts with materials by being blocked, transmitted, or reflected. Objects are classified as luminous or non-luminous based on whether they produce their own light. Reflection occurs on most surfaces, not just mirrors.
